subject: Civil Engineering
title: Recycled and Sustainable Pavements
description: Learn Recycled and Sustainable Pavements in one minute.

hook.text: America recycles more asphalt than any other material — 99% gets reused.

buildup.text: Reclaimed asphalt pavement is milled off old roads and mixed into new asphalt.

discovery.text: Rubber from recycled tires added to asphalt reduces cracking and road noise.

twist.text: Pervious concrete lets rain pass through — reducing runoff and recharging groundwater.

climax.text: Cool pavements reflect sunlight, lowering urban heat island temperatures by degrees.

punchline.text: The road of the future is recycled, porous, and cool. It's already here.

quiz.question: What percentage of asphalt pavement is recycled in the United States?

details.summary: Recycled pavements reuse existing road materials by milling old asphalt and incorporating it as reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) in new mixes, or by crushing old concrete for use as aggregate. These practices reduce virgin material consumption, landfill waste, and construction costs by 20-40%.
details.whyItMatters: Road construction consumes billions of tons of aggregate annually. Recycling pavement materials significantly reduces the environmental footprint and cost of maintaining the world's vast road networks.
takeaways: RAP can replace 15-50% of virgin aggregate and binder in new asphalt mixes
Full-depth reclamation pulverizes and stabilizes the entire pavement in place
Warm-mix asphalt reduces production temperatures by 30 degrees, saving energy

faq.question: How is old asphalt pavement recycled into new road surfaces?
faq.answer: Old asphalt is milled from the road surface, crushed, and screened to size. The reclaimed asphalt pavement is blended with virgin aggregate and new binder in a hot-mix plant. Modern plants can incorporate 30-50% RAP while meeting the same performance specifications as all-virgin mixes.

faq.question: What is full-depth reclamation of pavements?
faq.answer: A large machine pulverizes the existing asphalt and base material in place, blending them with a stabilizing agent like cement, asphalt emulsion, or foamed asphalt. The material is compacted and graded on site, then topped with a new wearing surface. It avoids hauling and disposal entirely.
